source.title: AutoInit: Automatic Initialization via Jacobian Tuning
source.authors: Tian-Yu He; Darshil Doshi; A. Gromov

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the reported CIFAR-10 training results.
record.tranche_reason: Compares initialization recipes and reports whether trained networks interpolate the original CIFAR-10 training set, bearing on V1's training-error outcome. It does not use the same initialization or training setup as the version's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training interpolation for ResMLP-S12 and VGG19_BN under two initialization recipes each. The Jacobian and kernel values used to assess or tune initialization are not separate training-error results. Other initialization and training claims in the introduction and references are cited prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: VGG19_BN trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 directly tests V1's training-error outcome using the same broad method and measure as its originals. Different initialization and augmentation recipes do not themselves make this a different method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: AutoInit automatically finds useful initializations with competitive performance for VGG and ResMLP. Both initialization conditions for each CIFAR-10 architecture are stated to interpolate the original training set. Competitive performance does not mean equal performance: AutoInit ResMLP reaches 74.0% ImageNet top-1 accuracy versus 76.6% cited for the original recipe, with training differences.
record.recipe_differences: Uses AutoInit, which tunes initialization hyperparameters through partial Jacobians, and compares it with original or PyTorch initialization. The reported CIFAR-10 training uses LAMB for ResMLP-S12 and SGD with momentum for VGG19_BN; the paper measures training accuracy with Mixup.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization recipe and architecture/optimizer differ across the reported comparisons; no training-error difference is stated.

fits_no_version.finding: Original and AutoInit ResMLP-S12 models trained with LAMB interpolate CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP-based image classifiers trained with LAMB can interpolate clean-label CIFAR-10 under the reported recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: AutoInit tunes partial Jacobian norms and forward kernels; the pre-BN MLP analysis compares criticality with and without residual connections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization tuning and residual connections can control signal-propagation diagnostics at initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical and numerical convergence bounds concern optimization of auxiliary initialization scalars using Jacobian losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AutoInit's convergence depends on its tuning loss, learning rate, and initial weight scale.

record.problems: Training interpolation is stated without a numerical training-error value or uncertainty. Training accuracy is measured with Mixup, while interpolation is described for the original training set; the text does not detail that measurement. Only CIFAR-10 is tested.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying training-error results were left out. Initialization diagnostic plots and cited findings were not extracted as training-error rows.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, model-size dependence, early stopping, and recipes leaving substantial training error.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depths and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.

Faster learning or greater trainable depth attributable to signal-preserving initialization; orthogonal-versus-Gaussian initialization and very deep plain tanh networks. Initialization diagnostics alone do not establish these outcomes.
Supervised training above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. The supplied text supports interpolation statements directly; the Mixup accuracy curves should not be interpreted as numerical original-set training-error measurements. Initialization comparisons also use separately selected learning rates and weight decay, preventing a clean attribution of training-speed differences to initialization.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, or the version's stated substantial-error cases. Training accuracy was measured with Mixup, although the text separately says both models interpolate the original training set.
